paragraphs: The site at this address sells procurement software to government, sold under the Euna name and covering sourcing, contracts, purchasing, and invoicing. It is aimed at public sector teams who need to spend carefully, contract quickly, and stay compliant.

Solicitations are assembled from stored documents, templates, and approved language rather than started fresh each time. Evaluators score and compare proposals on customizable digital scorecards instead of working through email chains, spreadsheets, and messaging apps. Suppliers register themselves, submitting required documents, diversity classifications, and commodity codes. Every contract action, approval, and workflow step is logged and timestamped.

The page describes the product as a full cycle solution used by thousands of government agencies. It also claims access to the largest supplier network in North America. On artificial intelligence, the page states that the software surfaces insights while the agency's own team takes the action.

quote.text: Procurement Software for the Public Sector
